passes.summary: Rates shock week (10-year 5.15%, December hike priced) and NVIDIA's CEO exit hang over tech into NVIDIA's 11-17 report; the night's best ideas are company stories with something still to come: AEVEX's misread beat, Corteva's broken guide, Cisco's margin-and-orders sale.

proposals.name: AVEX

signal.why: reported 2026-11-11 after close, reacted yesterday: gap +12.5% (+1.2 ATR), day +13.4%, +16.2% against XAR, volume 2.1x, EPS surprise -328%; missed estimates and still rose against XAR (bad news bought)
signal.chart: below the 50-day; under 200 days of history; +0.5 ATR from the 20-day, RSI 50; volume 0.7x; daily ranges of the 10 sessions before today 1.82x the 50 before; resistance 14.02 (50-day, +12.1%); support 8.95 (52-week low, -28.5%); ATR 1.38 (11.0%); hedge XAR: correlation +0.45, beta 1.67

proposals.reason: The EPS miss was a one-time $37.9M BlackSea tax charge; revenue, guide (+$120M at midpoint) and core non-Ukraine growth disproved the revenue-cliff bear case, and Friday gave back two-thirds of the pop on light volume with no news.

reasoning.what_changed: Q3 (11-11) showed core non-Ukraine revenue at $137M, passing Ukraine revenue for the first time; 2026 revenue guide raised to $820-840M from $700-720M (consensus about $753M), EBITDA guide to $128-132M. The headline GAAP miss is entirely a deferred-tax charge tied to the BlackSea purchase.
reasoning.story: The stock halved between Q2 and Q3 on the fear that Ukraine programs roll off into a cliff and on the Bloomberg Navy drone-boat story. The quarter shows the cliff being replaced faster than assumed; at about 13x 2026 EBITDA and 2x sales it is cheap for a drone name, with a thin 32.6M-share float and about 9% of it short. Automated feeds still headline 'weak earnings', so the market may not have finished reading the quarter.
reasoning.chart: Gapped +12.5% and closed +13.4% on 2.1x volume on 11-12, then -9.1% on 11-13 on volume about 60% below average; 12.51 holds above the pre-report close of 12.13. 50-day near 14.02 is the first level above; 52-week low 8.95. Daily ranges about 11%.
reasoning.coming: Analysts putting the guide into models (Piper already lifted its target to $15), possible first orders on the up-to-$400M single-award drone contract, short covering on a thin float. No company event scheduled in the window.
reasoning.case_against: Madison Dearborn is free to sell after the lock-up and has sold early before; BlackSea sellers hold stock priced at $27.50; management conceded no new GARC hull orders; Q4 implied revenue is a touch below Q3; drone names sell off together and tax-loss selling hits a stock 40% under its IPO. These are supply risks and they argue for size and a stop, not against a quarter that changed the story.

proposals.wrong_if: Madison Dearborn or another large holder announces a block sale or secondary offering, or AEVEX closes back below 12.13 (the pre-report close) on above-average volume, or a report confirms Navy or Army cuts to its programs beyond the GARC hulls already disclosed.
proposals.hedge_why: XAR (aerospace and defense ETF) is its best fit of the funds, correlation 0.45, beta 1.67; it takes out the defense-sector tape that has moved drone names together.

proposals.reason: A brand-new standalone management team broke an eight-week-old guide on a Brazil distributor glut that it says is still worsening, with no buyback possible until 2027 and Friday's bounce stalling below the reaction-day midpoint.

reasoning.what_changed: First report as a pure crop-chemicals company (seed spun off as Vylor on 10-01): Latin America sales -31% organic, 2026 EBITDA guide cut to $1.1-1.125B from about $1.3B set at the 9-15 investor day; Q4 EBITDA guided to about half of last year's with prices down high single digits.
reasoning.story: This is a credibility break, not a one-quarter miss: the guide new management gave eight weeks ago is gone, about $250M of product is stuck in Brazil's channel, generic Chinese competition is pressing prices on five products and acetochlor through Q1 2027, and the CFO would not reconcile an $800M cash drop. Tax rules from the spin bar buybacks this quarter, so the company cannot support the stock. Peers (FMC, Syngenta) confirm the Brazil problem is industry-wide and not ending.
reasoning.chart: Worst one-day drop on record (-24.3% on 11-12, 3.2x volume) to 9.19; Friday's +2.6% to 9.43 on no news stayed below that day's midpoint of 9.91. 9.14 is the lowest the standalone company has ever traded. Barely moves with any fund, so it is close to an outright short.
reasoning.coming: More target cuts and estimate revisions as models absorb the half-size Q4; any Brazil channel data; the 15-state PFAS suit challenging the spin as a fraudulent transfer can produce a headline at any time. Nothing from the company before the February call.
reasoning.case_against: It is down about 31% in a month at roughly 7x EBITDA, new targets ($10-11) sit above the price, Oppenheimer calls risk-reward favorable, and an insider purchase would set off a sharp bounce on 7% daily ranges. The lesson on gap trades asks what carries it forward: here the guide-break drift, Brazil still declining after quarter end and the absence of a buyer are that answer, so it stays a 3.

proposals.wrong_if: A director or the CEO buys shares (Form 4) inside the window, or the company announces an accelerated cost program or Brazil exit with numbers, or CTVA closes above 9.91 (the 11-12 midpoint) twice.

signal.why: reported 2026-11-12 after close, reacted today: gap -1.7% (-0.5 ATR), day -6.2%, -4.2% against XLK, volume 1.5x, EPS surprise +6%; beat estimates and still fell against XLK (good news sold)
signal.chart: below the 50 and 200-day; 50-day above the 200-day and falling (trend mixed); -2.0 ATR from the 20-day, RSI 37; volume 1.5x; daily ranges of the 10 sessions before today 1.80x the 50 before; resistance 101.74 (200-day, +6.4%); support 93.35 (20-day low, -2.4%); ATR 3.88 (4.1%); hedge XLK: correlation +0.72, beta 0.87

proposals.reason: A beat and raise was sold for reasons that last: gross margin down 2.5 points on AI mix and memory costs, product orders slowing from 35% to 21%, and the hyperscaler order figure no longer disclosed; analysts cut targets the next day.

reasoning.what_changed: FQ1 (11-12): revenue +24% and EPS $1.40 beat, full-year guide raised, but non-GAAP gross margin fell to 65.6% from 68.1% with the year guided just under 65%, product orders slowed to +21% (+14% excluding hyperscalers), Q2 revenue guide below Q1, and Cisco stopped reporting hyperscaler AI orders.
reasoning.story: The market is repricing Cisco from AI-networking winner to lower-margin hardware vendor whose orders were pulled ahead of price increases (Morgan Stanley's 11-05 downgrade said so). Dropping the order disclosure reads as hiding a weaker number, and a multiyear memory supply deal says the cost squeeze lasts. This is the third post-earnings drop in four reports.
reasoning.chart: Rallied about 9% into the print to the 101.60-102.71 resistance and failed; -6.2% on 11-13 to 95.64 on 1.5x volume, -4.2% against XLK; below the 50-day (107.6) and 200-day (101.7). Support 93.35 (20-day low) is 2.4% away, then 91.74.
reasoning.coming: Continued estimate trims on margins (Rosenblatt, Wells, Citi, Piper, Barclays already cut 11-13); NVIDIA's report 11-17 after the close sets the AI-hardware tape, which the XLK hedge partly offsets.
reasoning.case_against: Earnings guide raised about 8%, $6.1B of buyback authority, 17-18x forward earnings, support close below, and a good NVIDIA report could squeeze AI-hardware shorts. Hedged against XLK the trade is on Cisco's own margin and order story, which the market-wide bounce doesn't fix.

proposals.wrong_if: Cisco or a sell-side note discloses hyperscaler AI orders re-accelerating, or two or more brokers upgrade or raise targets on margin stabilising, or CSCO closes back above 101.60 (the failed resistance).
proposals.hedge_why: XLK (technology ETF) correlation 0.72, beta 0.87, the screen's best fit after MTUM; it neutralises the tech and NVIDIA-day tape.
